## What I found

You asked whether everything is pushed and whether the feature branch can be deleted. I can't answer either here: this working directory is not a git repository. There is no `.git` anywhere under `.`, and the only contents are `CLAUDE.md` plus the `.claude/skills/` library — no source code, no remote, no branches, no merge. Alchemy dispatched `SKIP` (a VCS state question asks no gate question), so the blocker is the missing repo, not a gate.

## Why it matters

Branch deletion is the one step here that discards information. If I guessed "merged, so yes, delete," and the merge was a squash whose tip commit never reached the remote, the only copy of that work would be the branch ref. Answering from the premise instead of from the repo is exactly the partial-success-reported-as-success failure that poisons the next decision. Nothing is lost by waiting for the path.

## Do this first

1. Tell me the real repo path (or `cd` there), and I'll run the checks. The three that actually decide it:
   - `git status -sb` — unpushed commits and dirty tree on the current branch
   - `git log --branches --not --remotes --oneline` — any commit on any local branch that exists nowhere on a remote
   - `git branch --merged <integration-branch>` — whether the feature branch's tip is genuinely an ancestor of what you merged into
2. If the merge was a squash or rebase, `--merged` will say "no" even though the work landed. In that case use `git cherry -v <integration-branch> <feature-branch>`; only `-`-prefixed lines mean "already upstream."
3. Delete with `git branch -d` (not `-D`) — the lowercase form refuses when the work isn't reachable, which is the safety check doing its job.

## What I did not check

Everything you asked about, because the repository is absent: push state, remote tracking config, whether the merge contains the branch tip, and whether other branches or open PRs build on it. All four are closed by the commands above once I have the path.
